payload.blocks: Only the 'life of an open question' section and its code; every other part of the shared communication rule keeps shaping.
payload.headline: How should a moot owner question leave your queue when its asker is gone?

parts.cause: Only the asker or a session holding its head role may cancel (refusal not-asker, questions spec section 5); askers rotate or end, and the store never looks at the plan behind a question's ref.

options.cost: About 60-100 lines Rust plus tests in packages/questions, spec section 5 edit.
options.does: Rule: asker withdraws a moot question. `fgos questions` marks a question whose plan or phase ref is done; the secretary may cancel a marked question.
options.gain: Clears the common case (plan done) even when the asker is gone; no watcher.
options.harm: Changes who may cancel (spec section 5); a moot question whose ref is not a plan still needs the asker.
options.label: A. Duty + done flag + secretary cancel

options.does: Rule: asker withdraws; whoever presents a question re-checks it against live state first. No code.
options.gain: Zero code; ships with the rule text.
options.harm: A gone asker leaves its moot question in the queue, today's case.
options.label: B. Prose duty only

options.cost: About 150-250 lines across supervision and questions.
options.does: A watcher detection raises an event when a ref's plan is done; the supervisor starts the asker's successor to cancel.
options.gain: Fully automatic, keeps cancel with the asker role.
options.harm: New detection and supervisor work; bigger than the problem.
options.label: C. Watcher event to the asker's successor

parts.recommendation: A: it clears the case that caused 5 of 8 moot questions with the smallest change and no new watcher. Default if no answer: shaping records A as provisional and the planner plans it; you can still pick B or C before the plan lands.

scope.allows: Recording the choice in DISCUSSION.md and handing it to a planner.
scope.forbids: Any code or spec edit now; the shaper edits only its discussion file.

parts.what: 5 of the 8 owner questions open on 2026-11-22 were moot (plan already done, already approved another way), yet stayed in your queue. The new shared rule needs a way to clear them.

payload.blocks: Only the program-check part; the prose rules keep shaping.
payload.headline: Should `fgos questions ask` require a stated default and a question headline?

parts.cause: The door (questions-input.v1.json) already checks headline length, 2-4 options, exactly one recommended and the scope; it has no field for a default and does not check that the headline is a question.

options.cost: About 40-70 lines (contract, Rust check, tests) plus skill text.
options.does: Add a required field: what the asker does, and when, if no answer comes. Headline must end with '?'. The store shows options as A-D itself.
options.gain: Every question you see states its default and reads as a question; askers write no letters.
options.harm: Every asker must fill one more field; old skills' examples change.
options.label: A. Require default + '?' headline, letter at render

options.does: The store letters options A-D; default and headline stay prose rules.
options.harm: Defaults stay missing whenever an agent forgets.
options.label: B. Letter at render only

options.does: No door change; all three are prose rules.
options.harm: Relies on every agent remembering; today's friction repeats.
options.label: C. Prose only

parts.recommendation: A: a stated default is the rule most often missed and the one that lets you answer with one letter or not at all. Default if no answer: A is recorded as provisional and planned.

scope.allows: Recording the choice in DISCUSSION.md and handing it to a planner.
scope.forbids: Any code or contract edit now.

parts.what: You answered fastest when options were lettered, one was marked, and a default was stated. The new rule asks for all three; the open question is which of them the ask door refuses when missing.
